No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

The lecture explains what counts as culture and what counts as heritage, and how the two differ. It works through tangible and intangible heritage with Indian examples, then looks at the institutions and communities that protect it, from UNESCO and the Archaeological Survey of India to the people who live beside a monument.

Length, level and language are agreed with you. The lecture can be given online or at your venue, for a single class, a department or a whole organisation.

What it covers

  • Culture and heritage: the difference, with Indian examples
  • Tangible and intangible heritage
  • Who protects heritage: UNESCO, the Archaeological Survey of India and local communities
  • Time for the group's own questions

How the time is spent

  1. What is heritage? 20 min

    Tangible, intangible, contested and lived heritage.

    You: personal inventory

  2. Who decides? 35 min

    Stakeholders, community knowledge and conservation.

    You: role discussion

  3. Public interpretation 20 min

    Translate research into accessible exhibit labels.

    You: draft interpretation

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Explain the difference between culture and heritage using Indian examples.
  • Distinguish tangible from intangible heritage, and recognise contested and lived heritage.
  • Identify who protects heritage, from UNESCO and the Archaeological Survey of India to local communities.
